subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Interviewing about future plans and the poem ‘Goodbye, School’
outcomes: Interview a classmate about future plans with full answers
Read and discuss a poem about leaving school
Share your own feelings about leaving school

tf.s: In an interview, you should answer only 'yes' or 'no'.
tf.why: Add details and reasons to your answers.

tf.s: Giving details keeps the conversation going.
tf.why: More information gives your partner more to ask about.

tf.s: The poet has mixed emotions about leaving school.
tf.why: The poet feels hope and affection at the same time.

tf.s: In the poem, 'patience' refers to the patience of teachers.
tf.why: The teachers patiently helped with learning.

tf.s: The poet only feels sad and has no hope for the future.
tf.why: The poet also feels hope for the future.

tf.s: The poet will remember close friends and the help of teachers.
The two lines students write about leaving school must rhyme.
tf.why: They do not need to rhyme.

tf.s: 'Prospects' are your chances of success in the future.
tf.why: Good prospects mean a hopeful future.

tf.s: An 'achievement' is something you have done successfully.
tf.why: Passing a hard exam is an achievement.

tf.s: Ambitions are things you want to forget.
tf.why: Ambitions are goals you hope to achieve.

boxes.q: What should you add to 'yes' or 'no' in an interview?
Which is one of the interview question headings?
boxes.why: The headings were job, university, travel and ambitions.

boxes.q: What does the poet feel about leaving school?
Whose patience does the poem mention?

boxes.why: Friends are a big part of school life.

boxes.q: Which is the best answer to 'Do you want to go to university?'
o: Yes, I want to study IT because I enjoy computers.
boxes.why: It gives a reason and more information.

boxes.q: How many lines do students write about leaving school?
boxes.why: A short poem of two lines.

o: a strong wish to achieve something
boxes.why: Your ambition is your big goal.

hunt.q: Staying calm while you wait or help
A strong wish for the future
Whose patience is in the poem?
Lines to write about leaving school

mcq.q: Why shouldn't you answer only 'yes' or 'no' in an interview?
o: To give more information and keep the conversation going
mcq.why: Full answers make a better interview.

mcq.q: Which four headings were used for the interview questions?
mcq.why: These headings are about future plans.

mcq.q: What does 'patience' refer to in the poem?
o: The patience of teachers who helped with learning
mcq.why: The poet is thankful to the teachers.

mcq.q: Which two feelings does the poet have?
o: Hope for the future and affection for school

mcq.q: Your partner asks: 'Do you want to travel?' Which answer is best?
o: Yes, I'd like to visit Japan to see its technology.
mcq.why: It gives a place and a reason.

mcq.q: Which question would you ask about ambitions?
o: What do you hope to achieve in the future?

mcq.q: Complete: 'Getting a scholarship was a great ___ for her.'
mcq.why: Getting a scholarship is a success.

mcq.q: Why might the poet feel both sad and hopeful?
o: Leaving means saying goodbye to friends but starting a new future
mcq.why: An ending is also a new beginning.

mcq.q: Why might the poet thank teachers for their patience?
o: They helped calmly with learning over many years
mcq.why: Patient teachers make a big difference.

mcq.q: Which interview answer gives the most useful information?
o: I want to be an engineer because I love designing things.
mcq.why: It gives a plan and a reason.
